## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: defensive driving and road rage
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The whole manual carries an old content-currency date (stated in part A), so any rule here may have changed since; the freshness debt in part A covers every fact in this section.
Physical page one hundred five is the Section C divider and carries only the section title, which is cited once [A01].
The extra following distance for interstates, large vehicles and bad weather is given here as at least three to four seconds, while the rules of the road chapter sets a minimum of four seconds for similar conditions; this chapter's wording is taught (verify TN-DEF-D-FOLLOW) [A03].
This chapter's general scanning distance is shorter than the scanning distance the interstate chapter gives for highway driving; the two are context-specific and are not merged.
The aggressive driving share of traffic deaths is credited to a federal agency without a year or citation, so it is held as a dated, unverified statistic (verify TN-DEF-D-STAT) [A05].

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 107 says to increase following distance to at least 3 to 4 seconds on high-speed interstates, behind large trucks or buses and in bad weather, while physical page 62 sets a minimum of four seconds for bad weather, high-speed interstates and night driving; confirm the recommended gap.

Physical page 109 credits NHTSA with saying about 66 percent of annual traffic fatalities are caused by aggressive driving; no year or source document is given, so the figure needs confirmation from NHTSA before learner use.
